connection: Session 7 established the prerequisite model. This session applies it to parameter passing modes with observable TimeClock examples.
objectives: Explain ordinary parameters copy their argument value, while ref, out, and in make aliasing or initialization explicit.
Predict behavior before running a focused parameter passing modes example.
Apply parameter passing with ref, out, and in without weakening existing domain invariants.
Verify the behavior with automated tests.

preQuiz.prompt: Which approach best explains parameter passing with ref, out, and in?
options: ordinary parameters copy their argument value, while ref, out, and in make aliasing or initialization explicit

preQuiz.explanation: The accurate model distinguishes identity, value, and API capability.

concept.title: Build the behavioral model
paragraphs: The central rule is that ordinary parameters copy their argument value, while ref, out, and in make aliasing or initialization explicit.
Names and syntax matter because they communicate whether code copies, aliases, enumerates, compares, or constrains a value.
concept.code:
ParameterExamples.TryParseHours("7.5", out decimal hours);
ParameterExamples.AddHour(ref hours);

concept.title: Program to the required capability
paragraphs: A caller should not need to provide more capability than the operation consumes.
Concrete implementations remain useful at construction boundaries; interfaces and generic contracts keep consuming code focused.
concept.code:
// Prefer the smallest contract that supports the operation.
ParameterExamples.TryParseHours("7.5", out decimal hours);

concept.title: Verify cause and effect
paragraphs: The lab changes one behavior at a time and uses tests to preserve the observation.
If the prediction differs from the result, explain the language rule before continuing.

lab.objective: Add a focused TimeClock example that demonstrates parameter passing with ref, out, and in.
lab.startingCondition: Sessions 01–07 are complete and the solution builds with all existing tests passing.
steps: Read the starting test and predict the result using the session mental model.
Add src/TimeClock.Domain/ParameterExamples.cs with the smallest API needed for the example.
Add tests/TimeClock.Domain.Tests/ParameterExamplesTests.cs to check the important before-and-after behavior.
Run the focused tests, then run the complete Release test suite.
Review whether each parameter and return type exposes only the capability it needs.
lab.expectedBehavior: The new tests demonstrate ordinary parameters copy their argument value, while ref, out, and in make aliasing or initialization explicit; all existing behavior remains green.
lab.validation: dotnet build TimeClock.sln --configuration Release && dotnet test TimeClock.sln --configuration Release

postQuiz.prompt: What did the lab establish about parameter passing with ref, out, and in?
options: ordinary parameters copy their argument value, while ref, out, and in make aliasing or initialization explicit
The compiler cannot describe the behavior
Tests replace the need for a mental model

postQuiz.prompt: Why run the entire suite after the focused test?
options: To detect regressions across cumulative code
postQuiz.explanation: The course application grows cumulatively, so earlier guarantees must remain intact.

postQuiz.prompt: When should a concrete collection or implementation leak into an API?
options: Only when its specific capability is part of the contract
postQuiz.explanation: Expose concrete capability only when callers genuinely need it.

reflections: How would you explain parameter passing with ref, out, and in without using a memory-location shortcut?
Which compiler error or test most clearly reveals the contract?
Where could an unnecessarily concrete type make future change harder?
whatBreaks: Removing the new domain example removes the executable model for parameter passing modes. Removing its tests allows subtle changes to assignment, equality, enumeration, or generic contracts to pass unnoticed. Widening the API unnecessarily gives callers capabilities the operation does not need.
summary: This session established that ordinary parameters copy their argument value, while ref, out, and in make aliasing or initialization explicit. The TimeClock example, tests, and API review turn that rule into durable engineering practice.
